items.followUp: What is test data? Explain normal and extreme test data.

rubric.why: Shows that test data is used to check a program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining test data as data entered into a program to check its operation or results.

rubric.why: Identifies ordinary valid input the program is expected to accept.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that normal test data consists of typical, valid values.

rubric.why: Identifies valid data at the edge of the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that extreme test data checks values at or near the limits of the valid range.

rubric.why: Identifies input that does not meet the program's acceptable conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that abnormal test data is invalid or outside the allowed conditions and checks how the program handles it.

modelAnswer: Test data is data entered into a program to check whether it works correctly and produces the expected results.
Normal test data consists of typical, valid values that the program is designed to accept.
Extreme test data consists of values at or near the upper or lower limits of the acceptable range.
Abnormal test data is invalid or outside the acceptable conditions and checks whether the program handles it correctly.

items.followUp: Name the four TCP/IP layers and describe the function of the Internet layer.

rubric.why: Names the Application layer and describes the services it provides.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating that it provides network services to programs or users.

rubric.why: Names the Transport layer and describes its delivery or segmentation role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and describing end-to-end communication or dividing data into segments.

rubric.why: Names the Internet layer and describes addressing or routing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating that it uses logical addresses or routes packets between networks.

rubric.why: Names the Network Access layer and describes transmission over the network link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating that it sends or receives data over the physical network link.

modelAnswer: The Application layer provides network services to programs and users, such as web and email services.
The Transport layer manages end-to-end communication and may divide data into segments for delivery.
The Internet layer uses logical addresses and routes packets between networks.
The Network Access layer sends and receives data over the physical network link.

items.followUp: Give two differences between an algorithm and a flowchart.

rubric.why: Identifies an algorithm as a written sequence of steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an algorithm is a written, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.

rubric.why: Identifies a flowchart as a graphical representation using standard symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a flowchart represents a solution graphically using standard symbols and arrows.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a written, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
A flowchart is a graphical representation of a solution using standard symbols and arrows.

items.followUp: What is the difference between an ordered list and an unordered list in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies the kind of list created by the tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that <ul> creates an unordered list, usually displayed with bullets.

rubric.why: Explains how entries are added to the unordered list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each entry is written using an <li> tag.

modelAnswer: The <ul> tag creates an unordered list, usually displayed with bullet points.
Each list item is written using an <li> tag.
